title: Block staff time and record operational disruption
summary: Keep non-bookable time visible and review appointments affected by disruption.

sections.title: Create a staff block
sections.body:
You need appointment-management access. Open **Calendar → More calendar actions → Block staff time**.

1. Choose **Staff** and **Type**: **Personal block** or **Staff break**.
2. Enter a clear **Calendar label**.
3. Set **Starts** and **Ends** in the location’s local time.
4. Enter the required **Private reason** and select **Create block**.
5. Check the block on the staff member’s schedule.

Choose time without an existing appointment or reserved slot. A block cannot be used to force another reservation out of the way.

sections.title: Record a disruption
sections.body:
For a visit running late, an overrun or unavailable staff, use the appointment’s operational-impact action. In **Record operational impact**, choose **Exception**, set **Projected end** where appropriate, enter **Reason** and select **Record impact**. Review the affected appointments for follow-up.

Authorized managers can use **More calendar actions → Record unexpected closure**. Set **Starts**, **Ends** and **Reason**, then select **Record closure** after checking the interval.

sections.title: Follow up with affected clients
sections.body:
Recording operational impact or an unexpected closure lists the affected appointments. Their times are not automatically moved or cancelled. Open each affected visit, agree a useful next step with the client and use the normal reschedule or cancellation workflow.

For recurring breaks, regular working hours or planned time off, use Team scheduling rather than creating many one-off blocks. Keep private reasons factual; calendar viewers see safe schedule labels rather than private leave explanations.
